Tycho Brahe is an astronomer. In 1572, Tycho noticed a completely new star that was brighter than any star or planet.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Ted Kaczynski is a mathematician. The FBI used the case identifier UNABOM (University and Airline Bombing) before his identity was known, resulting in the media naming him the "Unabomber".
What is the atomic number of Indium?
Indium: It is a silvery-white post-transition metal and one of the softest elements.
What is the atomic number of Scandium?
Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
In what year was Aristotle born?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year was Polyester discovered?
Polyester is a category of polymers that contain one or two ester linkages in every repeat unit of their main chain.
Information theory: Claude Shannon. Information theory is the mathematical study of the quantification, storage, and communication of a particular type of mathematically defined information.
Midazolam: Pfizer. It induces sleepiness, decreases anxiety, and causes anterograde amnesia.
In which country did the CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder take place?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: People's Republic of China. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Darmstadtium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Darmstadtium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Darmstadtium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Ds and atomic number 110.
Who is credited with discovering 2 Pallas?
2 Pallas: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Pallas (minor-planet designation: 2 Pallas) is the third-largest asteroid in the Solar System by volume and mass.
Who is credited with discovering Multiple sclerosis?
Multiple sclerosis: Jean-Martin Charcot. It is a type of demyelinating disease, where the nervous system's ability to transmit signals is damaged.
Which European four-engine turboprop military transport plane, sized between the Lockheed C-130 and Boeing C-17, can land on rough airstrips and double as an aerial refueling tanker?
Airbus A400M Atlas is a European four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft. It can carry heavier loads than the C-130 and can use rough landing strips.
Before sharing the 2010 Nobel for graphene, this Manchester physicist won an Ig Nobel for levitating a frog using its own magnetism — who is he?
Andre Geim (born 21 October 1958) is a Russian-born British physicist working in England in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Manchester.
Which noble gas, symbol Ar and atomic number 18, is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere — more plentiful there than carbon dioxide or neon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
This facial hair grows on the jaw, chin, and cheeks, most commonly in adult men, though some women develop it too in a condition called hirsutism — name it?
Beard is the hair that grows on the jaw, chin, upper lip, lower lip, cheeks, and neck of humans and some non-human animals.
Dermatologists call the small version of this fluid-filled skin pocket a vesicle and the larger version a bulla; its English name traces back to an Old French word for a leprous nodule. What is it?

Blister is a small pocket of body fluid (lymph, serum, plasma, blood, or pus) within the upper layers of the skin, usually caused by forceful rubbing (friction), burning, freezing, chemical exposure or infection.
This English guard-dog breed combines the size of the Mastiff with genes from the extinct Old English Bulldog, and gained Kennel Club recognition in 1924 — which breed?
Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
Which Mediterranean evergreen tree, grown mainly in Spain, produces edible seed pods often ground into a chocolate substitute, with seeds that yield a gum used as a food thickener?
Carob (Ceratonia siliqua) is a flowering evergreen tree or shrub in the Caesalpinioideae subfamily of the legume family, Fabaceae.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks and rays — has a skeleton made almost entirely of cartilage, setting it apart from its bony-skeletoned relatives. What class is this?

Chondrichthyes (from Ancient Greek (khndros) 'cartilage' and (ikhths) 'fish') is a class of jawed fish that contains the cartilaginous fish or chondrichthyans, which all have skeletons primarily composed of cartilage.
This towering annual in the daisy family yields seeds in two flavors — oilseed (the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil) and the confectionary kind you crack as a snack — which plant?
Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is a large annual forb in the daisy family Asteraceae.
This term describes all the material inside a cell's outer membrane, excluding the nucleus (in cells that have one) — its main components include a gel-like fluid called the cytosol. What is it?
Cytoplasm is all the material within a eukaryotic or prokaryotic cell, enclosed by the cell membrane, including the organelles and excluding the nucleus in eukaryotic cells.
Tamed in Africa millennia ago and still hauling loads across the developing world, which equine traces its lineage to Equus africanus?
Donkey is a domesticated equine. It was domesticated in Africa some 5000–7000 years ago, and has been used mainly as a working animal since that time.
The tallest native bird in Australia and the third-tallest living bird overall, this flightless ratite can grow up to 1.9 metres tall. What bird is it?
Emu (Dromaius novaehollandiae) is a species of flightless bird endemic to Australia, where it is the tallest native bird.

Mostly caused by a mutation in the PRNP gene, this neurodegenerative prion disease begins with gradually worsening sleep trouble and progresses to total sleeplessness, speech and coordination problems, and death within months — which disease?
Fatal insomnia is a neurodegenerative prion disease that results in trouble sleeping as its hallmark symptom.
Named after a German militant group in a reader's 1994 letter and formalized by a Stanford linguist in 2005, this cognitive bias makes newly learned facts seem suddenly everywhere — what is it?

Frequency illusion (also known as the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon or Red Car Theory) is a cognitive bias in which a person notices a specific concept, word, or product more frequently after recently becoming aware of it.
Caused in over 90% of cases by iodine deficiency, this visible swelling in the neck comes from an enlarged thyroid gland — name the condition?
Goitre (British English, spelled goiter in American English) is a swelling in the neck resulting from an enlarged thyroid gland.
A Hollywood star of Algiers and Boom Town, this Austrian-American actress also co-invented a wartime radio guidance system — who was she?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 - January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.

This condition occurs when cerebrospinal fluid builds up in and around the brain, in babies causing a rapid increase in head size and in the elderly causing poor balance and mental decline — what condition is it?
Hydrocephalus is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) builds up within and/or around the brain, which can cause pressure to increase in the skull.

This sudden bleeding into brain tissue or its ventricles is one of two major stroke categories, alongside the blockage-caused kind, and can trigger headache, one-sided weakness, or sudden speech and vision problems — what's the condition?
Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), also known as hemorrhagic stroke, is a sudden bleeding into the tissues of the brain (i.e., the parenchyma), into its ventricles, or both.
England's very first Astronomer Royal, he compiled a 3,000-star catalogue and even spotted Uranus — though he mistakenly logged it as a star. Who was he?
John Flamsteed (19 August 1646 - 31 December 1719) was an English astronomer and the first Astronomer Royal.
Native to southern China but long cultivated in Japan and Southeast Asia, this small fruit closely resembles an orange in color and texture but is only about the size of a large olive — what is it?
Kumquat are a group of small, angiosperm, fruit-bearing trees in the family Rutaceae.
Sociable for a big cat and more active by day than its relatives, this savannah hunter is so sexually dimorphic that only the males grow a sweeping mane. Which animal?
Lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

This German sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, which carried out what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — before the Nazis stripped his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
Magnus Hirschfeld (14 May 1868 - 14 May 1935) was a German physician, sexologist, and LGBTQ advocate whose German citizenship was revoked in 1933 by the Nazi government.
This natural biological transition marks the permanent end of menstrual periods, typically occurring between ages 45 and 55 as estrogen levels decline — what is it?
Menopause is the time when menstrual periods permanently stop, marking the end of the reproductive stage for the female human.
This Nissin Food Products founder invented instant chicken ramen and went on to create the Top Ramen and Cup Noodles brands — who is he?

Momofuku Ando (March 5, 1910 - January 5, 2007), born Go Pek-Hok (Peh-e-j: G Pek-hok; Ti-l: Go Pik-hok), was a Taiwanese-born, ethnic Chinese, Japanese inventor and businessman who founded Nissin Food Products Co., Ltd.

Distinguished from flatworms by having a digestive tract with openings at both ends, these free-living or parasitic roundworms make up their own entire phylum found in nearly every environment on Earth — what are they?
Nematode (or NEEM-; Ancient), roundworms or eelworms constitute the phylum Nematoda.
Founder of the charity Volnoe Delo and the industrial group Basic Element, which Russian oligarch led both En+ Group and Rusal until stepping down in 2018?
Oleg Deripaska (born 2 January 1968) is a Russian oligarch and billionaire.

Closely related to carrot and parsley, this pale, long-tapered root vegetable grows sweeter in flavor after winter frosts and produces yellow flowers if left unharvested into its second season — name the vegetable?
Parsnip (Pastinaca sativa) is a root vegetable closely related to carrot and parsley, all belonging to the flowering plant family Apiaceae.
Prized as an ornamental indoor plant and still poorly understood taxonomically, this arum-family genus ranks second in size only to Anthurium — which genus?
Philodendron is a large genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This birth defect results in extra fingers or toes, occurs more often in the hands than the feet, and has been linked to more than three dozen genetic mutations — what is it?
Polydactyly (commonly known as sixth finger and extra finger) is a birth defect that results in extra fingers or toes.

Also called blepharoptosis and sometimes mistakenly called 'lazy eye,' this condition is marked by the drooping of the upper lid over the eye and can affect vision development in children if untreated — what is it?
Ptosis (eyelid) is a drooping or falling of the upper eyelid.
This long-term autoimmune disorder leaves joints warm, swollen and painful — typically the same ones on both sides of the body — and can stiffen worse after rest. What is it?
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a long-term autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints.

Native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries have long been used for cordial and wine, and it also appears in traditional medicine and dietary supplements — name this plant?
Sambucus nigra is a temperate species of tree or shrub in the family Viburnaceae native to the Azores, Europe, and the Middle East.

Dubbed the "father of modern differential geometry," this Chinese-born American mathematician and poet won the Wolf Prize — and has a medal named for him by the International Mathematical Union. Who was he?
Shiing-Shen Chern (pinyin: Chn Xngshn; October 26, 1911 - December 3, 2004) was a Chinese-born American mathematician and poet.

Some versions allow a 'tie' or 'draw' while others insist on a single winner; it can pit hundreds against each other or just one person against the clock — what do we call this organized physical activity?
Sport is a physical activity or game, often competitive and organized, that maintains or improves physical ability and skills.
This West African berry contains a molecule that binds so powerfully to taste buds that sour foods eaten afterward taste sweet instead — what's this plant's common nickname?
Synsepalum dulcificum is a plant in the Sapotaceae family, native to tropical Africa.

One of five genera in the mackerel family whose members are collectively called tunas, this genus contains eight species, including the Atlantic bluefin, which can grow up to 15 feet long — name this genus?
Thunnus is a genus of ocean-dwelling, ray-finned bony fish from the mackerel family, Scombridae.
Caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria and contracted orally, this disease presents with gradual fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, rose-colored skin spots. What is it?
Typhoid fever is an orally contracted disease caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria, also called Salmonella Typhi.

In physics, this phenomenon occurs when two coherent waves combine according to their phase difference, producing either a boosted 'constructive' amplitude or a canceling 'destructive' one — what's the effect called?
Wave interference is a phenomenon in which two coherent waves are combined by adding their intensities or displacements with due consideration for their phase difference.
The second asteroid ever discovered and likely a leftover protoplanet, this object is the third-largest in the asteroid belt by mass — about 79% the mass of Vesta — what is it?
2 Pallas: Third-largest asteroid. Pallas (minor-planet designation: 2 Pallas) is the third-largest asteroid in the Solar System by volume and mass.
Known for the fused bony 'boss' across its forehead, this large, notoriously unpredictable Sub-Saharan bovine has never been domesticated — what animal is it?

Its seasonal form is called hay fever: a type I hypersensitivity reaction where the immune system overreacts to airborne allergens, bringing sneezing, a runny nose, and itchy, watery eyes — what's the medical name?
Allergic rhinitis: Nasal inflammation due to allergens in the air.
Considered the father of the exact and natural sciences in Armenia, this 7th-century polymath wrote the first known Armenian geographic work — who was he?
Most often caused by stroke or head trauma, this condition impairs a person's ability to understand or produce language because specific brain regions aren't working. What is it?
Aphasia: Inability to comprehend or formulate language.
This chronic airway disease causes wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath when triggers like pollen or dust make the bronchioles constrict and fill with mucus — what condition is it?
Asthma: Long-term inflammatory disease of the airways of the lungs.
The most common type of skin cancer, this slow-growing tumor is sometimes called a 'rodent ulcer' and rarely spreads beyond its original site — what is it?
Basal-cell carcinoma: Most common type of skin cancer. Basal-cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as basal-cell cancer, basalioma, or rodent ulcer, is the most common type of skin cancer.
Coined by Károly Ereky in 1919, this multidisciplinary field harnesses bacteria, yeast, and plants — often via genetic engineering — to create products and services. What field?
Biotechnology: Use of living systems and organisms to develop or make useful products.

Completely dependent on humans for reproduction after millennia of selective breeding, this domesticated moth's caterpillars produce the raw fiber behind a 5,000-year-old Chinese industry — which species?
Bombyx mori: Moth mainly used in the production of silk.

Prescribed under the tongue, as a cheek film, an injection, a skin patch, or an implant, this opioid treats pain and opioid use disorder — often combined with naloxone in Suboxone to deter injection misuse. What is it?
Buprenorphine: Opioid used to treat pain and opioid use disorder.
This golden fungus — also known as 'girolle' — is often confused with a poisonous lookalike, though it remains a prized edible mushroom and the type species of its genus — which one is it?
Cantharellus cibarius: Species of fungus. Despite its characteristic features, C. cibarius can be confused with species such as the poisonous Omphalotus illudens.
Marketed as Zinacef and used against everything from meningitis to Lyme disease, this second-generation cephalosporin antibiotic was patented in 1971 — which drug?
Cefuroxime: Antibiotic medication. It is used by mouth or by injection into a vein or muscle.
Nicknamed the sea wasp, this Australian box jellyfish is considered the world's most lethal, with venom-laced tentacles up to 10 feet long — which species?
Chironex fleckeri: Species of jellyfish. It has been described as "the most lethal jellyfish in the world", with at least 64 known deaths in Australia from 1884 to 2021.
This little Indo-Pacific reef fish, banded in white, shelters among stinging tentacles and repays the favor by fending off anemone-eaters and fanning its host clean. What fish is it?
Named after a Quechua word meaning the same thing, this New World vulture — with Andean and Californian species — is the largest flying land bird in the Western Hemisphere. What is it?
Condor: Name for two species of vultures.
Commonly called comb jellies, these are the largest animals that swim using rows of cilia, drifting through every ocean as masses of two-layered jelly — what's the phylum?
Ctenophora: Phylum of gelatinous marine animals.
This biological process, powered by rhythmic muscle waves called peristalsis, expels solid waste from the digestive tract through the anus or cloaca — what is it?
Defecation: Expulsion of feces from the digestive tract.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
One of the Hungarian émigré scientists nicknamed the "Martians," he extended Fermi's theory of beta decay and is colloquially called the father of the hydrogen bomb — who was he?

Dubbed a 'living fossil' and commonly known as horsetail, this spore-reproducing plant genus once included 30-meter-tall trees in Carboniferous forests, its node-spacing pattern said to have inspired the invention of logarithms — which genus?

With a rich chestnut crown and a bold black patch on each white cheek, this small Old World songbird nests in cavities, walls, or abandoned magpie nests, and lays five or six eggs that hatch in under two weeks — which bird?
Eurasian tree sparrow: Species of bird. The sexes have similar plumage, and young birds are duller versions of the adult.
Born Leonardo Bonacci in Pisa, this medieval Italian mathematician's 1202 book 'Liber Abaci' introduced Europe to Indo-Arabic numerals and a famous number sequence bearing his nickname — who is he?
Dubbed the "Flying Tailor," this inventor was so sure his wearable parachute would work that he leapt from the Eiffel Tower to test it himself — fatally. Who was he?
Dubbed "the Godfather of AI" for his pioneering work on neural networks, this Nobel laureate quit Google in 2023 to warn about AI's risks. Who is he?
Google's web mapping platform offers satellite imagery, live traffic and route planning, plus 360-degree interactive panoramas taken along roads. What is that panorama feature called?
Google Maps offers satellite imagery, aerial photography, street maps, 360-degree interactive panoramic views of streets known as Street View, real-time traffic conditions and route planning.
Created by a web server and stored by your browser, this small block of data is what lets a site remember your shopping basket or keep you logged in between page loads. What is it called?

An HTTP cookie is a small block of data a web server creates while a user browses a site, placed on the user's device by the browser, letting servers store stateful information such as items in a basket or whether the user is signed in.
Often contracted from undercooked shellfish or contaminated water, this foodborne viral liver disease causes symptoms like jaundice and fever that typically last around eight weeks — what is it?
Hepatitis A: Acute infectious disease of the liver.
This hormone, produced by cells surrounding a growing embryo, is what's detected in pregnancy tests and sometimes secreted by tumors, aiding cancer diagnosis — what is it?
Human chorionic gonadotropin: Hormone for the maternal recognition of pregnancy.

Named from the Greek word for "fish" because of its dry, scaly skin, this family of genetic skin disorders ranges from a mild type mistaken for ordinary dry skin to a rare, life-threatening form — which condition?
Ichthyosis: Family of disorders causing dry, thickened, scaly skin.

Native to the Americas but now grown worldwide, one species of this flowering plant genus has become such a popular ornamental that it's classified as an invasive weed on four continents — which genus?
Jacaranda: Genus of trees. The generic name is also used as the common name.
The youngest division chief in GM history shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the motor company behind a stainless-steel sports car immortalized in Back to the Future — who was he?
John DeLorean: American automobile engineer and executive (1925–2005)
Smaller, seedier, and more aromatic than its Persian cousin, this citrus hybrid lends its tart flavor to a beloved Florida pie named after the island chain it's associated with — what is it?
Key lime: Citrus fruit and plant.
Weighing up to 1,100 pounds, this heaviest of all non-crocodilian reptiles lacks a bony shell, its carapace covered instead in oily, leather-like flesh — what animal is it?
Leatherback sea turtle: Species of marine reptile.
Nicknamed for the Greek goddess of wisdom, this roughly 22-centimeter nocturnal bird was introduced to Britain in the late 1800s and to New Zealand's South Island soon after — which species?
Little owl: Species of owl. It was introduced into Britain at the end of the 19th century and into the South Island of New Zealand in the early 20th century.
Developed by MathWorks and named for its focus on matrix manipulations, this proprietary numeric computing environment powers the add-on Simulink for model-based design. What's it called?
MATLAB: Numerical computing environment and programming language.
Whether a milk board's 'Got Milk?' campaign or a city pitching itself as a tourist destination, this discipline boils down to acquiring, satisfying, and retaining customers — what is it?
Marketing: Study and process of exploring, creating, and delivering value to customers.
This WWII German monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe alongside the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, though Allied aircrew nicknamed it after its designer — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Bf 109: German WWII fighter aircraft family. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).

This Serbian polymath — mathematician, astronomer, civil engineer — explained Earth's long-term climate swings by tracking our planet's shifting position relative to the Sun, a theory of cycles that now bears his name. Who was he?
Milutin Milanković: Serbian scientist and professor (1879–1958)
This Bangladeshi economist founded Grameen Bank and pioneered modern microcredit, winning the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize before later leading an interim government — who is he?
Muhammad Yunus: Bangladeshi economist and statesman (born 1940)
Carried harmlessly in the noses of about 10% of adults, this bacterium is the only cause of bacterial meningitis known to occur in epidemics, especially across Africa and Asia — which microbe?
Neisseria meningitidis: Species of bacterium that can cause meningitis.

Introduced in 2001 and originally developed under the name Tier II+, which remotely piloted, high-altitude surveillance aircraft supports the US Air Force with long-endurance radar and infrared sensors?
Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk: Unmanned surveillance aircraft. It was initially designed by Ryan Aeronautical (now part of Northrop Grumman), and known as Tier II+ during development.
First domesticated in China's Yangtze River basin more than 8,000 years ago, this grass species is the world's most widely cultivated rice — which species?
Oryza sativa: Species of plant. Oryza sativa belongs to the genus Oryza and the BOP clade in the grass family Poaceae.
Believed to have originated in Sardinia and first cultivated in Britain in 1548, which herb is often used simply as a garnish today?
Parsley: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae cultivated as an herb.
Dubbed 'the champion of management as a serious discipline,' this Austrian-American writer popularized the concept of management by objectives — who is he?
Peter Drucker: American management consultant and author (1909–2005)
Also called threadworm in the UK and seatworm elsewhere, this common intestinal roundworm spreads via the faecal-oral route and is especially prevalent among children — what parasite is it?
A purplish-black crystalline salt that dissolves into an intensely pink-to-purple solution, this strong oxidizer also appears on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines for wound care — what is it?
This Greco-Roman scholar authored the Almagest on astronomy and the Geography, a treatise on maps and geographic knowledge — who is he?

In this condition, tiny arteries spasm and starve the fingers of blood, classically turning them white, then blue, then a burning red as flow returns. It's named for the physician who first described it in 1862 — what is it?
Raynaud syndrome: Medical condition in which spasm of arteries causes episodes of reduced blood flow.
Winner of the 1905 Nobel Prize for his tuberculosis research, this German physician's 1876 discovery of the anthrax bacterium is considered the birth of modern bacteriology — who is he?
Robert Koch: German physician and bacteriologist (1843–1910)

The largest living reptile, whose males can top 1,000 kg and stretch six metres, ranges from India's coast through Southeast Asia to northern Australia — and earns its 'dangerous to humans' reputation. Which croc is it?
Saltwater crocodile: Species of reptile. It has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 1996.
Ejaculated through the urethra and containing fructose plus enzymes that help sperm survive their journey to fertilize an egg, this bodily fluid is also collected for animal breeding. What is it?
Semen: Reproductive biofluid of male or hermaphroditic animals.

A parasomnia in which wakefulness and deep non-REM sleep occur in different brain regions at once, this condition can produce anything from bathroom trips to attempts at cooking or even driving — what is it?
Sleepwalking: Sleeping phenomenon combined with wakefulness.

Synthesized by Aristotle and taken as fact for two millennia, this superseded theory held that maggots could arise straight from dead flesh, until Louis Pasteur helped discredit it — what was it called?
Spontaneous generation: Theory of life arising from non-living matter.
Born from Russia's PAK FA programme begun in 1999 and carrying the internal name T-50, this twin-engine jet was the first Russian military aircraft built with stealth technology — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russian stealth multirole fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the brown raptor, this nocturnal bird of prey nests in tree hollows across Europe and is so territorial that evicted youngsters may starve — what is it?
Tawny owl: Stocky medium-sized owl species.

Marked by platelet counts that fall too low — sometimes below 50,000 per microliter and requiring emergency care — this blood disorder is the most common coagulation problem in ICU patients — what is it called?
Thrombocytopenia: Abnormally low levels of platelets in the blood.
This spiral-shaped bacterium, spread mainly through sexual contact and known only to infect humans and baboons, causes syphilis along with yaws and bejel — what is it?
Treponema pallidum: Species of bacterium. T. pallidum can enter the host through mucosal membranes or open lesions in the skin and is primarily spread through sexual contact.
Known as the Great Bear, this constellation contains the seven-star pattern nicknamed the Big Dipper — what's it called?
Ursa Major: Constellation in the northern sky.
This German experimental physicist shared the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physics with Max Born for the 'coincidence method' — the circuitry he used to study the Compton effect and cosmic rays. Who was he?
Sold under the veterinary brand name Rompun and often combined with ketamine for animal sedation, which structural analog of clonidine is this alpha2-adrenergic drug?
Xylazine: Veterinary anesthetic, sedative and analgesic.
Lutetium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for lutetium is Lu. Lutetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Lu and atomic number 71.
Titanium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for titanium is Ti. Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.

In what year was Frank Abagnale born?
Frank Abagnale: The book inspired the film of the same name, directed by Steven Spielberg in 2002, in which Abagnale was portrayed by Leonardo DiCaprio.
In what year was Bruce Lee born?
Bruce Lee (born Lee Jun-fan; November 27, 1940 – July 20, 1973) was a Hong Kong and American martial artist, actor, and filmmaker.
In what year was David Fincher born?
David Fincher: David Andrew Leo Fincher (born August 28, 1962) is an American director and producer.
In what year was Kate Winslet born?
Kate Winslet: Kate Elizabeth Winslet (born 5 October 1975) is an English actress.
In what year was Katee Sackhoff born?
Katee Sackhoff: Sackhoff also starred in the short-lived TV series The Fearing Mind (2000–2001) and The Education of Max Bickford (2001–2002).
In what year was Ringo Starr born?
Ringo Starr: Starr was afflicted by life-threatening illnesses during childhood, with periods of prolonged hospitalisation.
In what year was Tom Brady born?
Tom Brady: Brady is widely regarded as the greatest quarterback of all time.
In what year was Leonardo DiCaprio born?
Leonardo DiCaprio: Leonardo Wilhelm DiCaprio (Italian: [diˈkaːprjo]; born November 11, 1974) is an American actor and film producer.
In what year was Noah Baumbach born?
Noah Baumbach (born September 3, 1969) is an American filmmaker.
In what year was Liam Neeson born?
Liam Neeson: William John Neeson (born 7 June 1952) is an actor from Northern Ireland.
In what year was Alan Ritchson born?
Alan Ritchson: Alan Michael Ritchson (born November 28, 1982) is an American actor.
In what year did Kerry Von Erich die?
